features.title: Establish contracts, architecture, security, frontend foundations and agent workflow
features.story: As a team, we can develop independently against agreed secure contracts and consistent tools.
features.ac: All P01–P10 tasks are accepted; six hosts and one React client scaffold exist, contracts are approved, real bearer tests and CI work; foundations enable parallel service ownership.

features.title: Deliver the independently runnable Identity service and connected React views
features.story: As a signed-in player, I can see my own provider-backed profile without giving my identity-provider password to QuizArena.
features.ac: Six layer tasks completed with Domain/Data/Api separation, all specified REST and UI behavior, real OAuth bearer policies, persistence and negative tests. Identity runs independently and uses no other service assemblies or tables. GET /api/users/me => 200 profile, profiles.read; PUT /api/users/me => 200 profile, profiles.write, request {displayName:string}. Retire POST /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login with 410 ProblemDetails and documented OIDC redirect guidance; do not accept password payloads or mint tokens. GET /api/users/{id} is replaced by /me and returns 410 during documented transition. Frontend: ProfilePage.tsx: provider sign-in/sign-out buttons, current profile, display-name edit form; show 401 sign-in action, 403 permission message, field validation and saving state. No QuizArena password form.

features.title: Deliver the independently runnable Statistics service and connected React views
features.story: As a player, I can view my match history, totals and leaderboard, and only trusted gameplay can submit results.
features.ac: Six layer tasks completed with Domain/Data/Api separation, all specified REST and UI behavior, real OAuth bearer policies, persistence and negative tests. Statistics runs independently and uses no other service assemblies or tables. POST /api/results => 200 empty on first or identical retry, results.write service-only; conflicting duplicate =>409. GET /api/players/{userId}/stats =>200, stats.read and self; GET /api/players/{userId}/matches?page=1&pageSize=20 =>200, stats.read and self; invalid page/pageSize (1..100)=>400. GET /api/leaderboard?top=10 =>200, leaderboard.read, all signed-in players. Other user's self-only stats/history=>403. Frontend: StatisticsPage.tsx and LeaderboardPage.tsx: current player's totals, paged newest-first history, leaderboard top selector; empty-state text, loading/error/retry, no result-submission form.

features.title: Deliver the independently runnable QuestionBank service and connected React views
features.story: As a player, I can browse available quiz content, while Gameplay securely obtains the answer material needed for a real persisted match.
features.ac: Six layer tasks completed with Domain/Data/Api separation, all specified REST and UI behavior, real OAuth bearer policies, persistence and negative tests. QuestionBank runs independently and uses no other service assemblies or tables. GET /api/questions/generate?count=10 =>200, questions.read; count outside 1..50=>400; empty catalog=>200 []. POST /internal/question-sets {count:5} =>200 exact immutable snapshot, questions.play service-only; insufficient valid catalog=>409. No public DTO or Swagger browser sample exposes correct answers. Frontend: QuestionBankPage.tsx: question-count selector, generated question preview with options/category, regenerate button, empty/loading/error/validation states; never render correct answers or call /internal/question-sets.

features.title: Deliver the independently runnable Lobby service and connected React views
features.story: As a player, I can create or join a two-player lobby and, as its host, lock it before starting a match.
features.ac: Six layer tasks completed with Domain/Data/Api separation, all specified REST and UI behavior, real OAuth bearer policies, persistence and negative tests. Lobby runs independently and uses no other service assemblies or tables. POST /api/lobbies {} =>201, lobbies.write, Location points to GET; GET /api/lobbies/{joinCode} =>200, lobbies.read, sanitized join preview; POST /api/lobbies/{joinCode}/join {} =>200, lobbies.write; POST /api/lobbies/{joinCode}/lock =>200, lobbies.write plus host rule. Missing=>404; invalid joinCode=>400; invalid state/capacity=>409; nonhost lock=>403. GET /internal/lobbies/{joinCode} =>200, lobbies.verify service-only. Frontend: LobbyPage.tsx: create/join forms, join code display/copy, host/player membership and lock state; host-only lock/start controls, polling and cleanup; Start invokes Gameplay create after lock, displays navigation to returned match.

features.title: Deliver the independently runnable Gameplay service and connected React views
features.story: As one of two lobby players, I can complete a fair five-round persisted quiz match and see a result that reaches Statistics and Notifications.
features.ac: Six layer tasks completed with Domain/Data/Api separation, all specified REST and UI behavior, real OAuth bearer policies, persistence and negative tests. Gameplay runs independently and uses no other service assemblies or tables. POST /matches {joinCode} =>201, matches.write and lobby host; repeat same lobby=>200 same match. GET /matches/{matchId} =>200, matches.read and participant; GET /matches/{matchId}/next-question =>200 public question, matches.read and participant; finished=>409. POST /matches/{matchId}/answers {questionId:Guid,answer:string} =>200 {correct,playerAScore,playerBScore,roundComplete,finished}, matches.write and participant. Missing=>404; invalid input=>400; replay/stale/finished=>409; dependency unavailable before creation=>503 without partial match. Frontend: MatchPage.tsx: current public question/options, answer submit once, waiting-for-opponent display with polling, live scores, final winner/draw and links to stats/events. Hide answer key; disable duplicate submission and handle 409 refresh, 401/403 and network retry.

features.title: Deliver the independently runnable Notification service and connected React views
features.story: As a player, I can read my match events and manage my notification preferences without exposing another player's data.
features.ac: Six layer tasks completed with Domain/Data/Api separation, all specified REST and UI behavior, real OAuth bearer policies, persistence and negative tests. Notification runs independently and uses no other service assemblies or tables. POST /events {eventId:Guid,type,userId,payload:{matchId,winnerUserId?,draw?}} =>202 persisted EventResponse, events.write service-only; exact retry same response, conflict409. GET /events?page=1&pageSize=20 =>200 self events, events.read; legacy userId query if supplied must equal caller or403. GET /users/{userId}/preferences =>200 defaults/stored, preferences.read and self; PUT same route {emailEnabled,pushEnabled} =>200, preferences.write and self. Invalid payload/page=>400; cross-user=>403. Frontend: NotificationsPage.tsx: self event timeline with pagination/empty state and PreferencesPage.tsx with email/push toggles, save feedback and failures; explain that external delivery is not implemented, show only actual event records.

features.title: Integrate, validate, document and submit the reviewed GitHub milestone
features.story: As the team, we can demonstrate and submit a working, secure, tested multi-service product with real review evidence.
features.ac: D01–D08 accepted: clean startup, safe data cutover, complete browser E2E, 2–3-page reflection, traceable published board, actual peer signoff, merged milestone GitHub PR and retained milestone branch.

issues.title: Publish the milestone board, ownership map and GitHub delivery rules
issues.story: As a team, we need accountable work tracking and a safe milestone integration path before production implementation.
issues.files: docs/milestone3/work-allocation.md; docs/milestone3/workflow.md; .github/pull_request_template.md; GitHub Project and milestone metadata
steps: Verify collaborator logins/permissions, existing issues/PRs/milestones and main as the integration branch; link/reuse matching work items.
Record Jim=QuestionBank/Lobby, Carter=Identity/Statistics, Suheng=Gameplay/Notification with peer-review rotation; publish the board and dependency map.
Document milestone branch, task branch/PR targets, retained milestone branch, issue references, three human gates and GitHub submission URLs.
issues.ac: Board includes epic, all features/tasks, owners, milestones and dependencies; each member owns two runnable services and related UI. Current feature/milestone-3-layered-service-development already exists locally and on origin and currently matches main; verify ancestry before reuse, never recreate/reset it. New work only enters main through reviewed milestone PR. Source rubric mentions Azure DevOps/Lea; user explicitly selected GitHub, so use GitHub equivalents and record this override rather than provisioning Azure DevOps.
issues.verify: Inspect board URLs, owner fields, hierarchy, branch ancestry, template and traceability rules. Do not claim peer approval before a real human review.

issues.title: Approve service boundaries, public contracts, identity mapping and security policies
issues.story: As parallel implementers, we need committed contracts and explicit behavior so service and frontend changes agree.
steps: Review and approve every proposed architecture/product decision in this prompt, especially Keycloak, opaque subject/string match IDs, two-player/five-round rules and added endpoint scope.
Commit schemas, endpoint/status/policy matrix, service/client base URLs, error schema, pagination and idempotency rules before implementation fans out.

Define account mapping from legacy Guid IDs to (issuer,subject), machine identities, allowed scopes/audiences, match/event delivery contracts and version transition; collect all three members' approval.
issues.ac: Six owners' service contracts (two per member) and frontend routes are explicit; no public answer keys or client-selected current-user IDs. API DTOs and application interfaces live in each Api; Domain contains pure entities/rules. No service shares another service's assemblies or database tables. Changes to existing endpoints/IDs and account/password migration are documented. Architecture decisions are proposals until Gate 1 approval; issue creation itself does not approve them.
issues.verify: Contract review with all three members; compare OpenAPI with all leaf issue scopes, including positive/negative examples; every route has public/protected status and required named policy.

issues.title: Scaffold six independently runnable layered services and migrate the solution graph
issues.story: As a developer, I need independent service hosts and enforced project boundaries.
issues.files: QuizArena.sln; src/QuizArena.{Identity,Statistics,QuestionBank,Lobby,Gameplay,Notification}.{Domain,Data,Api}/*.csproj; each Api/Program.cs and Properties/launchSettings.json; tests/QuizArena.ArchitectureTests/
steps: Create 18 net10.0 backend projects and six pairs of per-service test projects; add to solution with unique host entrypoint types/namespaces.
Create composition roots, configurable ports and unauthenticated GET /health endpoints; migrate code incrementally into the owned projects without duplicating runtime ownership.

Add architecture tests for Domain with zero NuGet/outer/web dependencies, Data->own Domain only, Api->own Data/Domain only, no cross-service project references; coordinate removal of obsolete aggregate projects in D02.
issues.ac: All six hosts build and each launches with its own configuration/port even when peers are down; /health verifies liveness, not downstream dependencies. Dedicated Domain/Data/Api projects exist for every service; a mere namespace split or six contexts in one API is insufficient. Pure services do not depend on HTTP DTOs. No frontend backend-assembly references. Architecture tests fail for prohibited references.
issues.verify: dotnet build QuizArena.sln --no-restore -warnaserror; run architecture tests; launch each Api and request /health with other APIs stopped.

issues.title: Establish service-owned EF configuration, migrations and safe database boundaries
issues.story: As a service owner, I need independently managed persistence without accidental cross-module table access.
issues.files: each src/QuizArena.<Service>.Data/{Context,Configurations,Migrations}/; each Api connection-string configuration; docs/milestone3/database-operations.md; .config/dotnet-tools.json
steps: Use SQL Server provider with six development databases QuizArena_<Service>; each service connects only to its own database and owns its migrations/history.
Extract unified context mappings into owned IEntityTypeConfiguration classes; preserve documented indexes, required columns and intradomain cascade/restrict rules; add design-time factories.

Document explicit per-context migrate commands, startup/readiness, unique test databases, credentials from environment/secrets and non-destructive old-database retention. Leave actual data transfer to D02.
issues.ac: No cross-service foreign keys, navigation properties or shared context survive final cutover; legacy QuizArenaDb is preserved during migration. Six migration lineages apply to empty databases. No schema is initialized in production with EnsureCreated. Connection credentials are never committed. Service-specific schema constraints are completed by the corresponding data task.
issues.verify: For each service: dotnet ef database update --project src/QuizArena.<Service>.Data --startup-project src/QuizArena.<Service>.Api --context <Service>DbContext; inspect owned tables and relational constraints.

issues.title: Configure a reproducible OIDC provider and client/service identities
issues.story: As a user and service caller, I need standard OAuth/OIDC tokens with intentional access grants.
steps: After approval of Keycloak in P02, configure realm quizarena, public quizarena-client using authorization code + PKCE S256 and exact redirect/logout origins.
Register resource audiences and least-privilege service identities/scopes from the matrix; configure player scope grants without exposing internal scopes.
Provide reproducible local startup/realm setup, provision users/secrets outside Git, disable password grant/implicit flow and document client/resource owner/authorization server/resource servers.
issues.ac: Browser has no client secret and never sends an IdP password to QuizArena. Gameplay confidential client may request lobbies.verify/questions.play/results.write/events.write with only corresponding audiences; browser gets none. Test fixture keys are ephemeral; production signing credentials absent. Approved issuer/audience/HTTPS settings vary by environment; development HTTP relaxation limited to Development.
issues.verify: Manually demonstrate provider login/PKCE redirect, minted access-token audience/scopes and negative insufficient-grant cases; document metadata/JWKS locations and setup without recording tokens or secrets.

issues.title: Apply real JWT validation and reusable scope policies to all six APIs
issues.story: As a resource owner, I need every API to validate tokens and enforce least privilege independently.
steps: Use Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer with configured authority/audience; validate signature, issuer, audience, lifetime and signing keys; UseAuthentication before UseAuthorization.
Implement exact scope membership for space-delimited scope and supported scp claims; apply explicit named policies and service-principal requirements. Use validated sub/iss for user ownership.
Set authenticated fallback policy; explicitly allow /health and Development-only documentation; configure scoped CORS for approved frontend origin and safe ProblemDetails responses.
issues.ac: Each host rejects missing/invalid/expired/wrong-issuer/wrong-audience tokens with401, valid insufficient/wrong scope with403, valid required scope succeeds; ID tokens are not accepted as access tokens. Browser tokens cannot call internal ingestion even if a test token includes a scope without service identity. Scope substring matches never authorize. Public /health works without token. Ownership checks supplement scopes. No mock auth replaces real bearer validation in the security suite.
issues.verify: Per-service parameterized security matrix using ephemeral signing keys and local metadata fixture, including bad signature, expired token, unknown key, wrong issuer/audience, absent/wrong scope, authorized scope, public route and spoofed identity.

issues.title: Build the shared React frontend shell, OIDC session and HTTP clients
issues.story: As a player, I need one connected browser client for all six services.
steps: Scaffold React+TypeScript with Node/npm tooling, routing and navigation for profile, questions, lobby, match, statistics, leaderboard, events and preferences.
Implement PKCE provider login/logout/session refresh and bearer HTTP clients with independently configurable base URLs for six APIs; memory-only tokens, no browser client secret.
Provide reusable field validation, loading/empty/error/retry/401/403 displays, abortable requests and component test setup. Screens themselves belong to feature frontend tasks.
issues.ac: Use React from the requested MERN-style stack; .NET APIs own all persistence, no MongoDB is required. Node/npm supplies frontend tooling; no second Express business API or direct SQL access. Browser communicates only by REST and public DTOs. Distinct service ports work with CORS. Logout clears client state. Refresh failure returns user to sign-in without infinite retry.
issues.verify: npm ci; npm run typecheck; npm run lint; npm run build; npm run test -- --run in src/QuizArena.Client; test auth redirect, bearer attachment, refresh failure and common error components.

issues.title: Add constrained layer agents and reconcile the repository skills with Milestone 3
issues.story: As an AI-assisted developer, I need agents that respect service/layer boundaries and human gates.
steps: Create valid agent frontmatter, real supported tool allowlists, user-invocable names and service-scoped context; Domain/Data/Api/Client writing boundaries are explicit.
Update tests to per-service paths and Moq/xUnit/FluentAssertions; relational persistence coverage uses isolated SQL Server, not EF InMemory as constraint evidence.

Make review agent read-only; remove nonexistent skill tool names, stale aggregate layout and instruction to patch during read-only review; use specs/milestone3/<issue>-plan.md and three real human gates.
issues.ac: All four layer agents plus testing/review agents exist with linked readable skills; at least two layer agents and one testing/review skill satisfy the rubric. Domain agent cannot add EF/Web dependencies; Data cannot reference Api; frontend cannot reference backend assemblies; testing agent runs baseline before changes and edits tests only. Cross-layer changes are handed to the appropriate agent. Review reports severity but cannot edit/approve/merge. Existing useful workflow is retained with consistent paths.
issues.verify: Inspect frontmatter/tool validity and dry-run one bounded research/plan example per role; verify file access constraints and absence of contradictory test paths/providers.

issues.title: Create isolated per-service test hosts and a real bearer-token test fixture
issues.story: As a developer, I need deterministic tests that catch relational and security regressions.
steps: Migrate current service tests to their owned projects, preserve scenario coverage and record an actual baseline rather than copying historical 35-test results.
Build service-specific WebApplicationFactory hosts, unique SQL Server databases, per-test reset/seeding and reliable cleanup; mock outbound HTTP for focused integration tests.
Generate ephemeral signed test JWTs and local discovery/JWKS metadata for real JwtBearer; support service/user identities and negative token permutations without bypassing production policies.
issues.ac: Unit tests use Moq and no actual database; relational tests use the SQL Server provider and verify constraints. No test touches developer databases or depends on order. Existing fixture hidden DisposeAsync concern is resolved using deliberate lifecycle ownership. Framework InMemory tests are moved/reclassified when they exercise repositories. Every service has separate test results; new feature tests are added in feature test tasks.
issues.verify: Run all six unit/integration projects independently and together; verify repeated execution starts clean; run security fixture negative controls; cleanup removes only generated test databases.

issues.title: Add CI gates for architecture, backend, frontend and security tests
issues.story: As a reviewer, I need reproducible automated evidence before accepting any milestone PR.
steps: Provision a documented Windows SQL Server LocalDB environment or explicit SQL Server test instance; verify prerequisite availability and fail clearly rather than skip tests.
Restore/build with warnings treated as errors, verify formatting, run every test project and publish generated reports as CI artifacts.
Run locked frontend dependency install, typecheck/lint/tests/build, architecture tests and auth suites; configure required checks and keep secrets/build/coverage output untracked.
issues.ac: CI covers all six APIs and frontend; no silent skipped integration/auth tests, no production secret files, zero warnings/errors/failing tests required. Runtime/dependency/tool versions are pinned to supported compatible versions and lockfiles committed. Required-check names match branch protection. Test reports and redacted diagnostics are downloadable.
issues.verify: A real PR pipeline passes; deliberate architecture or test failure blocks merge. Commands match the shared validation contract and successful run URL is recorded.

issues.ac: No silent dropped data, coerced identities, invented provider subjects or password migration into IdP. Invalid mock matches remain archived rather than offered as playable real matches. Rerun import creates no duplicates. Six contexts enforce only their owned schemas; no runtime repository references QuizArenaContext. Backup/rollback is documented and source data deletion needs separate explicit approval.
issues.verify: Dry-run plus disposable-database rehearsal, before/after table counts, idempotent second run and rollback rehearsal; search source/solution for obsolete project/context references.

issues.title: Verify the complete secured two-player journey and delivery retries
issues.story: As a reviewer, I need evidence that the six independently running services work together through the browser.
steps: Use Playwright with two authenticated player contexts and real running services/provider to create/join/lock lobby, play five rounds, and view history/leaderboard/events/preferences.
Exercise bad/expired tokens, wrong scopes, user spoofing, unauthorized internal endpoints and answer-key leakage; confirm calls use HTTP instead of shared assemblies.

Interrupt downstream Statistics/Notification delivery, restart Gameplay, restore peers and verify pending retries produce exactly one result per player and one event per lifecycle recipient; test simultaneous submissions and draw.
issues.ac: One complete win and one draw journey pass; both players answer once per round, scores persist after restart, unauthorized caller cannot affect another player. Completion data eventually reaches both downstream services, duplicates do not accumulate. No browser internal credentials or answer keys. Record actual test counts, durations, run URLs and failures/remediation.
issues.verify: Run npm run test:e2e with isolated environment and dotnet test QuizArena.sln; archive redacted results/screenshots as generated CI artifacts.

issues.title: Write the Milestone 3 architecture, security and reflection report
issues.story: As an assessor, I can verify the architecture, work allocation and human/AI collaboration evidence.
steps: Update current architecture/service/data/API docs while marking Milestone2 plans/review counts as historical; link independently runnable projects and React integration.
Write a concise 2–3-page equivalent report covering layering, frontend choices, two services/member, agent assistance/manual corrections and defects caught by human gates.
Include OAuth actors/PKCE flow, redacted token settings, full endpoint-policy mapping, actual security tests, board/PR/plan/review links and GitHub-over-Azure submission decision.
issues.ac: Report is in the existing lowercase docs folder, linked from root README rather than creating a competing Docs tree; its rendered length is checked for 2–3 pages. Evidence is real, no fabricated AI corrections or signoffs. SQL ownership, no direct frontend storage and no cross-service assembly references are accurate. All required deliverable URLs are collected.
issues.verify: Peer-read report against rubric; validate links, endpoint names and current solution. Render/check page count or document the Markdown-to-PDF rendering settings used.

issues.title: Audit issue traceability, acceptance evidence and board completeness
issues.story: As the milestone owner, I need every requirement traceable to completed, reviewed work.
steps: Map every numbered rubric section and deliverable to actual feature/task numbers, PRs, tests and docs.
Audit each member's two complete vertical slices, all frontend tasks, dependencies and issue/PR references.
Publish board export or durable evidence and reconcile statuses with actual human-gate completion, leaving pending items open.
issues.ac: No orphan task, missing owner, missing frontend/test task or false Done status. Every required deliverable has a real URL. Blocked/remaining work is named explicitly; completion requires both acceptance and human gates.
issues.verify: Machine-readable issue map/export counts match epic/feature checklists; manually follow one full trace per member.

issues.title: Complete read-only review and human signoff for the milestone candidate
issues.story: As a peer reviewer, I need confidence in security, layering and test quality before merging.
steps: Run the constrained Code Review agent read-only over the complete milestone diff; capture category/severity/file/action in the established format.
Owners resolve all critical/high findings through linked issues/PRs and rerun affected checks; justify any lower-risk deferral with a concrete follow-up issue.
Have at least one other human member review each PR, verify all three gates/security checklist and record dated signoff with identity and CI evidence.
issues.ac: Automated review does not count as human approval. No unresolved critical/high findings; missing real approval remains blocked. Every service/feature has owner plan approval, post-implementation inspection and independent pre-merge review. Review agent modifies no files.
issues.verify: Inspect review records, latest successful CI and actual GitHub approvals; reviewer must differ from author; remediate stale approvals after substantive changes.

issues.title: Merge the retained milestone branch through a reviewed GitHub milestone PR
issues.story: As the milestone owner, I need one reviewed submission PR covering all Milestone 3 work.
steps: Verify all milestone changes are on feature/milestone-3-layered-service-development; update from main without destructive reset and resolve conflicts through review.

On first push only use git push -u origin feature/milestone-3-layered-service-development; open GitHub PR to main with epic/feature/task links, Milestone 3 title, summary, test results and human signoff log.
Obtain real peer approval and passing checks, merge according to repository rules, disable automatic deletion for this branch and verify the milestone branch remains after merge.
issues.ac: No direct push to main, no fabricated approvals, no premature merge. One milestone-level GitHub PR exists even when task PRs already exist. Source instructions' Azure DevOps destination is overridden by explicit user choice. Retain branch after merge and preserve all traceability links.
issues.verify: Record PR URL, base/head, merged commit, latest CI and independent approval; verify remote milestone branch still exists.

issues.title: Publish the final GitHub milestone submission bundle and board export
issues.story: As the submitter, I need the exact final evidence links ready for course submission.
issues.files: docs/milestone3/submission.md; GitHub Project export/evidence; epic completion comment
steps: Collect repository URL, board URL/export, merged task/milestone GitHub PRs, architecture/reflection report and validation/security evidence.
Confirm every feature/task meets closure criteria and update epic checklists/statuses truthfully.
Prepare the merged GitHub milestone PR URL for Lea submission; the human submitter performs course-system submission unless separately authorized.
issues.ac: Bundle contains all rubric deliverables using GitHub equivalents. No Azure DevOps setup task is created. Board/issue states reflect real completion; retained branch and milestone PR are verifiable. Lea submission is not falsely claimed.
issues.verify: Open every final link as a reviewer and verify report/board evidence remain accessible; owner acknowledges submission bundle.
